newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks seen treading water.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks seen treading water.

text.p: Argentine stocks were seen little changed at the opening Monday despite a new rally on Wall Street, dealers said.

"The market will probably continue to mark time ahead of this week's U.S. inflation data, because most players are sitting on the sidelines and won't step in now before they know what the Federal Reserve will do with interest rates," said Gabriel Ruiz of brokers Tavelli.
The Fed meets May 20 and traders said U.S. inflation indicators due out Wednesday and Thursday would help predict any action on interest rates.

Local stocks were seen selective as the results period winds up, with footwear and textile firm Alpargatas, for example, likely to be hit by news Monday it posted a first-quarter loss of $39.4 million.

"The stock will probably suffer but any drop should be temporary, because the company is undergoing a streamlining process and may even be sold, meaning its prospects are good much like happened with (steelmaker) Acindar," said Luis Diaz at Cohen traders.
The blue-chip MerVal index dipped 0.4 percent Friday to 723.78 and fell 1.2 percent in the week.
But Diaz predicted stocks would keep a firm underlying tone and move higher once they consolidate in the near term.
"I'm optimistic, and I think (bellwether) YPF will be able to rise above its record high," he said.
He added that the results of another market heavyweight, oil holding company Perez Companc, were in line with expectations. Perez announced a $72 million profit in the first quarter earlier Monday.
